summary: Gregor Ahn is a scholar of religious studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Copenhagen and Bonn (under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit), later holding posts at Münster, Tartu, and as professor at Heidelberg University from 1996 to 2025.

Gregory A. Hillis specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA at the University of Virginia in 1993, with an affiliation there attested in 2002, and serves as Continuing Lecturer at UC Santa Barbara (attested 2026).

Gregory Adam Scott works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Columbia University and has held posts at the University of Edinburgh and as Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester (both attested 2026).

Gregory Forgues works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and Birgit Kellner, and also studied under traditional teachers Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche, Namkhai Norbu, Thich Nu Tri Hai, and U Janakabhivamsa.

Gregory Max Seton specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa, UC Santa Barbara, and Oxford (Wolfson College), where his doctoral supervisors were Vesna A. Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.

Gregory P. A. Levine is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College and Princeton University before joining UC Berkeley around 2003 as Associate Professor of Japanese Art, Architecture, and Buddhist Visual Cultures.

Gregory Price Grieve works in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at San Francisco State University and the University of Chicago, later lecturing at Chicago and DePaul before becoming Professor and Head of Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro in 2002.

Gregory Schopen works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Black Hills State, McMaster, and the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana, he held professorships at Indiana, UT Austin, and UCLA.

Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Moscow State University, where he studied under George de Roerich, he held appointments at the Institute of Oriental Studies, MSU, the Institute of World History, and the Russian Academy of Sciences.
Gritli von Mitterwallner was an Indologist and historian who completed her doctorate and habilitation at the University of Munich, where she later served as Professor from 1978 to 1991.
Gu Rong Gyalsé Chökyi Lodrö studied under Thubten Chökyi Dorje, Terton Sogyal, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Guang Xing specializes in Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS, University of London, under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy H. Barrett. He became Assistant Professor at the University of Hong Kong (~2003) and visited UBC in 2007.

Guangchang Fang is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He served as a researcher at the Institute of Asia-Pacific Studies, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1987–2004), and became a professor at Shanghai Normal University (~2004).
Guankong was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He taught at the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute and served as a professor at the Buddhist Academy of China in 1957.

Gudo Wafu Nishijima was a Buddhist studies figure who held a law degree from the University of Tokyo and studied under Kodo Sawaki and Rempo Niwa. He lectured at Toho Gakuin and the University of Tokyo Buddhist Youth Association.

Gudrun Bühnemann specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Münster, Bonn, and Vienna (under Ernst Steinkellner), held fellowships in India and Japan, and became Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992.

Gudrun Melzer is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann. As of 2026, she holds research posts at Munich, Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and IIBS.
Gunapala Dharmasiri is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who held posts at the University of Ceylon, attested in 1991 and 2008.
Gunilla Gren-Eklund is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied under Stig Wikander and held a post at Uppsala University from approximately 1978 to 2003.
Gunnar Jarring was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Lund University from 1926 to 1933 and held an academic post there from approximately 1933 to 1940.
